channel.title: Kubernetes on Aashish Sheshadri
channel.description: Recent content in Kubernetes on Aashish Sheshadri

item.title: The Cluster That Learned to Plan Ahead
item.description: Why reactive autoscaling breaks at scale, and what happens when you teach a cluster to think ahead.

item.title: Why 1,500 HPAs Is Not an Autoscaling Strategy
item.description: Three failure modes of HPA at scale: cascade propagation, stampede scaling, and priority inversion.

item.title: Commander and Soldiers: Decomposing the Scaling Problem
item.description: Decomposing cluster-wide autoscaling into a Commander (budget allocation) and Soldiers (per-domain execution) using hierarchical RL.

item.title: Inside the Commander: What It Sees and What It Decides
item.description: The Commander's observation vector and action space, the telemetry lag underneath both, and why the budget is a share of CPU rather than a replica count.

item.title: What the Evals Missed
item.description: Stage gates, calibration by slice, and the reward-hacking detector I built three weeks too late. How I knew the system was working, and every place that knowledge turned out to be wrong.
